title: Lone working, harassment and personal safety on site
audience: Cleaning operatives, supervisors and managers who work alone, after hours, or in public-facing buildings.
learningOutcomes: Decide when lone working is avoided, and set up the buddy or supervision arrangement where it is not.
Describe the check-in and monitoring arrangements that apply to a lone worker.
Respond to harassment, a threat or a trespasser without escalating the situation.
Report an incident of harassment or violence to the named contacts.

instruction.heading: When lone working is avoided
instruction.body: The register's first control for lone working is to avoid it where that is possible. Where a task cannot be done without a second person, a buddy system is applied, so that two people share the work and can summon help. Where possible a site supervisor is present, and the client's security or reception staff monitor the cleaning employee on site. A regional supervisor looks in on crews at their sites. Senior staff decide whether a particular lone worker faces a risk, and that decision is recorded. The register does not allow a lone worker to be sent to a location without a check-in. A lone worker who cannot make contact at the agreed time is treated as a potential incident until the check-in is made.

instruction.heading: Harassment, threats and violence
instruction.body: Harassment and violence can come from the public, residents, site staff or others. The register's approach is to stop the work, secure the area, inform the client, the building facilities team and the business head office, and be polite. The operative does not retaliate or try to make the situation worse, because a calm response is the one most likely to end it. The business investigates a reported incident, and notifies the client and any regulator where appropriate. WARNING: Leave the area as soon as it is safe to do so. Do not confront anyone, do not block a door, and do not stay in a place where you feel unsafe.

instruction.heading: Trespassers and unfamiliar people
instruction.body: If someone is found on the premises without permission, the crew does not challenge them, does not follow them and does not try to remove them. The crew politely requests that they go, if it is safe to do so, and then reports the event to the building facilities team. A locked or unfamiliar area is not entered alone to investigate. The site contact is told, and the report records the time, the location and a description of the person without any attempt to identify them beyond what is seen. Personal safety is always placed above the cleaning task.

procedure: Check whether the task can be done with a second person or with supervision, and arrange that first.
Set up the check-in times with the named contacts before the lone task begins.
If a person is harassing or threatening, stop the work, move away and secure the area as far as possible.
Inform the client, the building facilities team and the business head office, and do not retaliate.
Do not challenge a trespasser. Request politely that they go if it is safe, and report the event.
Record the incident with the time, location, people involved and actions taken, and keep it confidential.

workedExamples.situation: After hours, a crew member is cleaning an office floor alone when a visitor enters and becomes angry about the cleaning schedule and moves closer.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: State the first response, the people who are told, and what is recorded.
workedExamples.reasoning: The crew member stops the work, steps back toward the exit and keeps a clear route open, and speaks calmly without arguing. The crew member does not block the visitor or confront them. The building's security or reception is contacted, and the crew member leaves once it is safe. The client, the building facilities team and the business head office are informed, and the incident is recorded with the times and the people involved.

equipmentAndPpe: Mobile phone or radio for check-ins and emergency calls
Check-in schedule and the named contact list for the site
Incident report form and the contact list for building facilities team
{{business:safety.emergency_contact}} and {{business:safety.escalation_contact}} written down before lone work

commonErrors.error: Starting a lone task without the check-in arranged.
commonErrors.prevention: Set the check-in times with the named contacts before starting, and do not begin without them.

commonErrors.error: Confronting a trespasser or an angry visitor.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, move away, and request politely that they go only if safe. Then report.

commonErrors.error: Not reporting an incident because it did not cause injury.
commonErrors.prevention: Report every harassment, threat or trespass event so the pattern can be seen and managed.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: WARNING: Do not confront any person who is trespassing or threatening. Leave the area, make a report and let the appropriate people deal with the person.
Check the duties to manage the risk of violence and the notification requirements for workplace violence and lone work under state and territory law.

qualityStandard: Lone work is avoided where possible, and check-ins are set before any lone task begins.
Every harassment, threat or trespass event is reported to the named contacts.
No one confronts a trespasser or retaliates against a visitor.
documentationEvidence: Lone work decision record, signed by the director or manager responsible
Incident report with the times, people, actions and notifications
summary: Avoid lone work where possible, and arrange a buddy or supervision where it is not.
Set check-ins before a lone task and treat a missed check-in as an incident.
Stop, move away and do not confront or retaliate.
Report every event to the named contacts, and record the notifications.

knowledgeChecks.question: A cleaner is asked to work alone in a building after hours. What does the register say about the first step?
options: Go alone, since the building is empty and the crew will check in later on the phone today
Start the task and call in later and then tell the office when it is all done and the building is locked up
Avoid lone working where possible, and arrange a buddy or supervision where it is not possible to avoid.

knowledgeChecks.question: A visitor becomes threatening during a clean. What is the correct first response?
options: Stop the work, move away, keep a clear exit, and contact the named contacts.
Argue calmly until the visitor leaves and keep the lift door open
Block the visitor's path to the lift and keep the visitor in view

knowledgeChecks.question: A trespasser is found in a locked area of the building. What should happen?
options: Escort the person out of the building and lock the doors behind them and check the area
Do not challenge them, request that they go if safe, and report the event to building facilities team.
Enter the area alone to check the trespasser's reason and ask them for their name and address
